intro: Pharmacies are everywhere in Cabo San Lucas, and most travelers buy sunscreen, stomach remedies or allergy tablets without a second thought. But news reports in recent years about counterfeit pills sold in some tourist-area shops have made many visitors ask a fair question: how do I know the medicine is real?
This guide explains what to look for in a pharmacy, which medicines need a prescription in Mexico, the red flags to avoid, and how to have genuine medicines delivered to your room.

list: A licensed establishment with its health authorization visible.
Sealed, original packaging with a lot number and expiry date — never loose pills in a bag.
Prices on a receipt, and a pharmacist willing to answer questions.
Prescriptions required for antibiotics and controlled medicines. A shop that skips this is a warning sign.
Strong prescription-only medicines offered without a prescription
Street vendors or shops pushing “pharmacy” deals to tourists
Pills sold out of the box or in unlabeled containers
Prices that seem far too low for brand-name medicines
p_after: If something feels wrong, do not buy it. Your health is worth more than the savings.

sections.h2: Do you need a prescription in Mexico?
p: For most everyday products — pain relievers, antacids, oral rehydration salts, after-sun care, allergy tablets — no. Antibiotics do need a prescription from a doctor licensed in Mexico, and a prescription from home is not enough. Our doctors can see you at your hotel ($189) or our clinic ($99) and write it the same day. Learn more on our pharmacy in Cabo San Lucas page.

sections.h2: Bringing medicine home to the US
p: Keep medicines in their original packaging with your receipt and, for prescription medicines, a copy of the prescription. Rules for bringing medicines into the United States can change, so check the current guidance from US Customs and the FDA before you fly, especially for controlled medicines.

faq.q: Are pharmacies in Cabo San Lucas safe?
faq.a: Licensed pharmacies that sell sealed, original medicines with a receipt are a safe choice. Avoid street vendors, loose pills and shops that sell prescription medicines without a prescription.

faq.q: How can I tell if medicine in Mexico is fake?
faq.a: Buy only sealed, original packaging with a lot number and expiry date, from a licensed pharmacy that gives you a receipt. Unusually low prices and missing packaging are warning signs.

faq.q: Can I buy antibiotics without a prescription in Cabo?
faq.a: No. In Mexico antibiotics require a prescription from a doctor licensed in Mexico. Our doctors can see you the same day and our pharmacy delivers the medicine.
